input.ground_truth: Germanic was an ethnic group long before the company of Germany was formed. Germany is really just the latest iteration in a chain of German countries in that area of the world. The Holy Roman Empire was the first "germany", but even before that the Romans would refer to that part of the world as Germania.

So, putting it all together, during Martin Luther's time, there was no unified Germany. Instead, the region was part of the Holy Roman Empire, which was a loose collection of territories. People identified more with their local area or ruler than with a national identity. Therefore, Martin Luther would have been considered a citizen of his local region or the Holy Roman Empire, not as a German in the modern sense.
